key: Fain to bring light to homes of men the noble and active Goddess hath emerged from darkness.
s: A hymn to Dawn opens with the Daksina’s broad chariot harnessed and the immortal Gods aboard; Sāyaṇa, on 1.123.1, reads the Goddess’s purpose as healing, a cure she works on the dwellings of men by driving away the darkness of night.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.123.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 348392 (2022)

evidence.words: अनन्तरं सा उषाः "कृष्णात् निकृष्टवर्णात् नैशात् तमसः सकाशात् "उदस्थात् उत्थिता अभूत् … मानुषाय "क्षयाय मनुष्याणां निवासाय “चिकित्सन्ती अन्धकारनिवारणरूपां चिकित्सां कुर्वती तमो निवारयन्तीत्यर्थः
evidence.gloss: Then that Dawn rose up from ‘the black’, the base-coloured darkness of night … ‘for the human abode’, for the dwelling of men, ‘cikitsantī’: performing a cure whose form is the warding off of darkness; that is, she wards off the dark.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 1.123.1, at [122,1]), the second sentence of the verse. Sāyaṇa on 1.123.1 glosses cikitsantī as performing a cure (cikitsā) whose form is the removal of darkness, for the dwelling of men (manuṣyāṇāṃ nivāsāya), and the darkness she rises from as that of night (naiśāt tamasaḥ); Wilson’s translation (‘bringing health to human habitations’) and his note (‘healing, remedying the malady of darkness’) agree. Plain sense draws on the verse’s first sentence as context and repeats no four words of the key; faithful. Revision 348392 is dated 2022-08-29 by the Wikisource API, so the src year stands. entry-check ok.
